change: move config/cyber-topics.json out of data/, where the Railway volume was mounting over it and hiding it from the container

checks.name: nothing the server reads is hidden by the volume
checks.expect: OK - nothing the server reads is hidden by the volume

checks.name: the taxonomy still verifies from its new home
checks.expect: OK - the taxonomy verifies, and a second implementation agrees with it

checks.name: a runtime module reading from data/ again is caught
checks.expect_failure: FAIL  no runtime module resolves a path into a shadowed directory
checks._why: This is the defect itself, restored. It passes every repository-side check: the path is valid, the file would be tracked, nothing is gitignored. Only a rule about the MOUNT can see it, so that rule has to be provably able to fire.

checks.name: the guard noticing a tracked file under data/ is proven, not assumed
checks.expect_failure: FAIL  the file detector flags a file under the mount, and clears one outside it
checks._why: A guard with an empty target list passes everything. Pointing it at a directory that does not exist proves the list is what the checks actually read.

checks.name: the loader resolves outside the mount, asked rather than read
checks.command: node -e "const t=require('./lib/cyber-topics'); const p=t.FILE; if(/[\\\\/]data[\\\\/]/.test(p)) throw new Error('the taxonomy is back under the mount: '+p); if(t.topics().length!==24) throw new Error('not 24 topics'); console.log('LOADER RESOLVES OUTSIDE THE MOUNT: '+p.split('/').slice(-2).join('/'));"
checks.expect: LOADER RESOLVES OUTSIDE THE MOUNT: config/cyber-topics.json
checks._why: The suite scans source text. This asks the loader where it actually points, so a change that satisfies the scan without moving the file is still caught.

checks.name: the boot seed reports ok and the 24 cyber rows are finally in production
checks.command: sh -c 'curl -sS https://progress.apcsexamprep.com/api/health | node -e "let s=\"\";process.stdin.on(\"data\",d=>s+=d).on(\"end\",()=>{const j=JSON.parse(s);const m=j.seed&&j.seed.seeds&&j.seed.seeds.course_manifest;if(!m)throw new Error(\"no course_manifest seed report\");if(!m.ok)throw new Error(\"the seed still fails: \"+m.error);if(m.total!==932)throw new Error(\"seeded \"+m.total+\" rows, expected 932\");console.log(\"LIVE SEED OK total=\"+m.total+\" changed=\"+m.changed)})"'
checks._why: False before this deploy in two independent ways: the seed reports ok:false with an ENOENT today, and the 24 rows are absent. The first deploy of this taxonomy asserted a count and could not say why it was wrong; this asserts the seed's own report AND the count, so a pass means the rows landed and the seed agrees that they did.
